The puzzle turns on a pun on "courses." The narrator is a HKU student who had to choose "courses" before a deadline, but these were not academic classes—they were the courses (dishes) of a meal at a university dining hall.

The student deliberately took part in choosing meal courses for that evening's dinner, so their own voluntary action played a causal role; it was not an administrative drop, a system bug, another student grabbing the classes, or someone else using their account. Crucially, the scenario is set in a dining hall: the student was selecting which dishes/courses they would have for the evening meal.

Because the "courses" were food dishes, they could be "gone" in the ordinary culinary sense—consumed, used up, or no longer available. Thus the apparent mystery "all of my courses were gone in one evening" is resolved by realizing that "courses" means the courses of a meal, not academic modules. The student's course choices were food selections at the dining hall, and by that evening the dishes were gone—the pun is that a student normally worries about losing places in academic courses, whereas here the lost "courses" were meal courses.
